concepts.title: Diversity in the Living World
concepts.definition: A single garden after rain shows dozens of different plants, insects and birds; the living world is richly diverse, and noticing this variety is the first lesson of biology.
concepts.key_idea: No two living things are exactly alike: diversity is the signature of life.

concepts.title: Grouping by Features
concepts.definition: To handle diversity we group living things by shared features, leaf shape, stem type, number of legs, wings or habitat; the chosen feature is the basis of the grouping, and a different basis gives different groups.
concepts.key_idea: Classification is a lens: pick a feature, and order appears in the variety.

concepts.title: Habitats of Plants and Animals
concepts.section: Plants and animals in different habitats
concepts.definition: Every living thing makes its home in a habitat, a pond, a desert, a forest or the sea, whose water, light and food suit its body; fish cannot live where cacti thrive, and each is fitted to its own place.
concepts.key_idea: Habitat decides who lives where: bodies are matched to the places that feed and shelter them.

concepts.title: Comparing and Recording Observations
concepts.definition: Careful study means comparing, relating and analysing: measure and draw leaves, compare two birds, relate a beak to its food, and record everything in tables and drawings so patterns stand out.
concepts.key_idea: Records turn watching into science: compared and tabulated observations reveal what memory alone would miss.
